concerns.text: FR-007/FR-008 require detection of matching Participant IDs across the composite datasets (ds000208 + ds003392). The reopened tasks drop the reward‑feedback dataset entirely and only inspect a single cohort, so the design‑type detection logic can never satisfy the spec’s cross‑dataset ID‑matching clause. This is a silent narrowing of the functional requirement.
FR-000 mandates validation of *both* datasets and their shared variables. T003 only downloads and validates ds000208, never the second dataset, thereby weakening the variable‑validation requirement.

SC-002 defines runtime as the sum of `duration_ms` fields from GitHub Actions step logs. T013 records only an in‑process wall‑clock timer, so the verification step cannot confirm compliance with the spec’s success criterion.

The `analysis_results.schema.yaml` requires each sensitivity entry to contain a numeric `power_at_alpha`. T009 produces only boolean significance flags, leaving the contract unfulfillable and violating the success‑criteria coverage.

Constitution VI demands that every external citation be verified by the Reference‑Validator Agent. No task in the list creates or runs such a verification step, so the pipeline would breach the constitution’s verified‑accuracy gate.

The dataset schema includes a mandatory `task` field (enum ['cyberball','reward']), yet no ingestion or preprocessing task ever creates or populates this column. Validation against the schema would inevitably fail, weakening FR‑000.
